summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the new Forgot-Password (Emergent Resend) flow. Backend: 24/24 pytest tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_forgot_password.py covering (a) POST /api/auth/forgot-password enumeration safety (identical 200 body/status for known and unknown emails, DB record created only for known emails, rate-limit blocks 6th call within the hour), (b) POST /api/auth/reset-password rejection paths (short password 400, non-6-digit code 400, wrong code 400, expired code 400+auto-purge, code reuse after success 400, >5 wrong attempts 400+invalidate), (c) success path (200 with {ok,token,user}, reset record removed, bcrypt-hashed password stored, ledger 'password_reset_completed' event appended, old password → 401, new password → 200), (d) _assert_safe_email guardrail rejects <form>/<input>, http://, bit.ly shorteners, IP-literal hosts, credential-ask phrases, while the real _reset_email_body template passes, (e) send_email helper no-ops + logs a warning when EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY is empty and POSTs to https://integrations.emergentagent.com/api/v1/email/send with X-Email-Key header + from_name when the key is set (mocked), (f) regression /api/auth/admin/reset-password still returns 503 / 401 / 200 correctly. Frontend: /auth/login shows testID='forgot-password-link' between Sign-in and 'or' divider — tap navigates to /auth/forgot-password with the typed email pre-filled. /auth/forgot-password renders the email input, 'Send reset code' button and 'I already have a code' link — submit shows the 'Check your inbox' confirmation with testID='continue-to-reset' which navigates to /auth/reset-password with the email carried in the query param. /auth/reset-password has all 4 inputs, code field only accepts digits and hard-caps at 6 (verified via typing '1234567890' → '123456' and typing 'ab123' → '123'), all client-side validations produce the correct messages ('Enter your email', 'Enter the 6-digit code from your email', 'Password must be at least 8 characters', "Passwords don't match"), backend 400 surfaces as 'Invalid or expired code' in testID='reset-error'. Full E2E: seeded a fresh reset code in Mongo, filled the UI, submitted → auto-login via useAuth().login → router.replace('/(tabs)/console') landed at /console with the tab bar rendered. Demo password restored to pocketos123 after the flow. NO bugs found.
action_items: None — feature is production-ready pending EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY provisioning at deploy. In preview the send_email helper correctly no-ops and logs 'send_email: EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY not set — email to <addr> NOT sent' as expected.

Reminder for main agent: pytest.ini pins '-n 2 --dist loadscope' — the new test file MUST be run with '-n 0' (serial) because parallel workers race on the shared demo@pocketos.app user's password_resets record. This is documented in the test file's docstring.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is >3400 lines — should be split into modules (auth, notes, council, ledger, decisions, forgot-password) for maintainability. Not blocking the current feature.

Rate-limit + forgot-password buckets (_FORGOT_ATTEMPTS, _ADMIN_RESET_ATTEMPTS) are in-process dicts. Fine for single-instance preview, but a Redis-backed limiter is safer once the app runs behind >1 replica.
seed_data_creation: Test seeded a temporary password_resets record with code '424242' for demo@pocketos.app to complete the UI E2E flow. Record consumed by the successful reset; demo password reset by the flow was restored to pocketos123 post-run and verified via /api/auth/login → 200.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_forgot_password.py -v --tb=short -n 0` (serial). Parallel xdist workers race on the shared demo user record. The tests are self-cleaning (each restores demo pw + purges password_resets records in a finally block). Test file uses direct in-process imports of server.py for seeding + guardrail tests, and public-URL requests to /api/auth/... for HTTP endpoint validation. Guardrail + send_email + admin-reset regressions are all covered.
rca_of_issue: Not applicable — feature validation, no bug found. Verified guardrail (_assert_safe_email is called on every send path including when EMAIL_KEY is empty — the guardrail runs BEFORE the empty-key early-return, so any bad template would still be caught). Enumeration safety verified byte-for-byte: known and unknown email responses have identical JSON bodies + identical 200 status.
